claims.text: A W-Ti-V-Cr refractory high-entropy alloy can be used as a low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
W, Ti, V, and Cr constitute a set of low-activation alloying elements suitable for the proposed application.
The proposed material is polycrystalline.
The proposed material may be in an irradiated initial state.
Adjusting the W-Ti-V-Cr elemental ratios can balance low activation, irradiation resistance, and high-temperature mechanical properties.
The proposed operating-temperature range is 500-1000°C.
The proposed irradiation-dose range is 10-100 dpa.
Grain-boundary structure and composition play a crucial role in the alloy's irradiation resistance.
Grain-boundary structure and composition play a crucial role in the alloy's high-temperature mechanical properties.
Optimized composition and grain-boundary structure reduce the formation of radiation-induced defects.
Optimized composition and grain-boundary structure improve high-temperature strength.
Optimized composition and grain-boundary structure improve high-temperature toughness.
Optimized composition and grain-boundary structure improve high-temperature creep resistance.
The W-Ti-V-Cr alloy will improve irradiation resistance by 20-30% relative to traditional structural materials.
The W-Ti-V-Cr alloy will improve high-temperature strength, toughness, and creep resistance by 15-25% relative to traditional structural materials.
The W-Ti-V-Cr alloy will reduce activation level by 50-70% relative to traditional structural materials.
Stainless steel and tungsten are traditional structural materials used in fusion reactors.
Alloy composition and processing conditions must be carefully controlled to obtain the desired properties.
The optimal W-Ti-V-Cr composition and processing conditions are unknown and require further research.
The W-Ti-V-Cr alloy's behavior under extreme irradiation conditions is not yet fully understood.
